title: Deploy the personal website's post editor as a loopback-only unit
objective: The website repo now ships a browser post editor. Give it a home on the server: a systemd unit bound to 127.0.0.1, started by setup_personal_website.sh, with credentials generated once and no public route. Success is that after a setup run the editor answers on 127.0.0.1:4321/admin, survives a reboot, and is reachable from a laptop only through an SSH tunnel.
acceptance_criteria: setup_personal_website.sh builds the editor and fails if either half of the build is missing.
Credentials are generated once, stored as a scrypt hash in a 0600 env file, and are not rotated by a second setup run.
The unit binds to loopback, runs under ProtectSystem=strict with the checkout as its only writable path, and still completes a real build.
No Caddy snippet, no firewall opening, and no reference to the editor on the public domain.
The setup report prints the tunnel command and the path of the password file, never the password.
out_of_scope: Any public or Tailscale route for the editor.
TLS for the editor: the SSH tunnel terminates on localhost, which browsers already treat as a secure origin.
Changes to the website container, the shared Caddy edge, or the Gitea relocation.
verifier: pre-commit run --files <the four shell files>; meta/scripts/shell_coverage_jail.sh over linux_configuration/features/lib/tests/test_website_admin.sh with --fail-on-case-error; systemd-analyze verify and a systemd-run rehearsal of the sandbox.
